_comment: Requirement catalogue for the educational simulator. These are demonstration software requirements, NOT real spacecraft requirements. Tests reference them with @pytest.mark.req(...).

REQ-BOOT-001.text: Simulator powers on in BOOT mode with no telemetry and payload OFF.

REQ-BOOT-002.text: INIT with an accepted, non-violating telemetry frame passes the self test and enters NOMINAL.

REQ-BOOT-003.text: INIT without any accepted telemetry is rejected with NO_TELEMETRY and the mode stays BOOT.

REQ-BOOT-004.text: INIT with telemetry that violates a safety rule enters SAFE_MODE, not NOMINAL.

REQ-BOOT-005.text: A failed power-on self test (injected SELF_TEST_FAILURE) enters FAULT.

REQ-CMD-001.text: Each non-blank, non-comment input line produces exactly one JSON response with response_seq, command, status, mode and sim_time_s.

REQ-CMD-002.text: Unknown commands are rejected with UNKNOWN_COMMAND and logged as COMMAND_REJECTED.

REQ-CMD-003.text: Command arguments are validated; invalid arguments are rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT without changing state.

REQ-CMD-004.text: Commands not permitted in the current mode are rejected with NOT_PERMITTED_IN_MODE according to the documented permission table.

REQ-CMD-005.text: Malformed input (oversized lines, control characters, non-ASCII bytes) is rejected with MALFORMED_INPUT without crashing.

REQ-CMD-006.text: Command names are case-insensitive; blank lines and '#' comments produce no response.

REQ-CMD-007.text: Repeated commands behave deterministically (ENTER_SAFE_MODE is idempotent, repeated STATUS is consistent).

REQ-MODE-001.text: A safety violation in NOMINAL transitions to SAFE_MODE with the violated rule recorded as the reason.

REQ-MODE-002.text: The ENTER_SAFE_MODE ground command transitions NOMINAL to SAFE_MODE.

REQ-MODE-003.text: EXIT_SAFE_MODE returns to NOMINAL only when no safety violation is active; otherwise it is rejected with ACTIVE_VIOLATIONS.

REQ-MODE-004.text: FAULT can only be left with RESET CONFIRM, which goes to BOOT (never directly to NOMINAL or SAFE_MODE).

REQ-MODE-005.text: The reported mode is never NOMINAL while a safety violation is active.

REQ-MODE-006.text: The payload can only be powered in NOMINAL and is forced OFF when leaving NOMINAL.

REQ-MODE-007.text: Every mode change is logged as a MODE_CHANGE event with from, to and reason.

REQ-TLM-001.text: A complete, valid telemetry frame is accepted and returned by GET_TELEMETRY.

REQ-TLM-002.text: Frames missing any required field are rejected with MISSING_FIELD.

REQ-TLM-003.text: Non-numeric, non-finite or physically implausible values are rejected (INVALID_ARGUMENT / OUT_OF_RANGE) and counted.

REQ-TLM-004.text: Frame sequence numbers must strictly increase; replayed or out-of-order frames are rejected with STALE_SEQUENCE.

REQ-TLM-005.text: Telemetry older than telemetry_timeout_s (strictly greater) raises TELEMETRY_STALE.

REQ-SAF-002.text: TEMPERATURE_HIGH trips strictly above temp_max_c; TEMPERATURE_LOW trips strictly below temp_min_c.

REQ-SAF-004.text: A frame with sensors=INVALID raises SENSOR_INVALID and its numeric values are not used for value rules.

REQ-SAF-005.text: No ground contact for longer than comm_timeout_s raises COMM_TIMEOUT and SAFE_MODE; communication loss never causes FAULT; shorter drops only produce warnings.

REQ-SAF-006.text: Value rules use hysteresis: an active violation clears only at its recover threshold.

REQ-SAF-007.text: Multiple simultaneous violations are all reported and each must clear before recovery is allowed.

REQ-REC-001.text: After all violations clear, EXIT_SAFE_MODE restores NOMINAL and the payload can be re-enabled.

REQ-REC-002.text: RESET CONFIRM from FAULT returns to BOOT with volatile state cleared; INIT then reaches NOMINAL.

REQ-CFG-001.text: A valid configuration is loaded and its thresholds are applied (custom thresholds change behaviour).

REQ-CFG-002.text: Missing, corrupt, incomplete or contradictory configuration is rejected with exit code 3 and a structured error.

REQ-CLI-001.text: Exit codes, --help, --version and --validate-config behave as documented.

REQ-CLI-002.text: stdout contains only JSON responses; diagnostics go to stderr or --log-file.

REQ-CLI-003.text: A missing script file or unwritable log file gives exit code 4 and a structured error.

REQ-LOG-001.text: Every log entry has log_seq, sim_time_s, severity, component, event, mode, message and details; log_seq is contiguous from 1.

REQ-LOG-002.text: Identical inputs produce byte-identical responses and logs (determinism).

REQ-REG-001.text: Golden reference scenarios produce exactly the recorded responses and log events.

REQ-FI-001.text: Every documented fault-injection scenario (scenarios/*.json) behaves as specified.
